title: How-to: Create a Hosted canary rollout in staging (end-to-end test)
author: Jada Williams
content:
This page describes the canonical staging flow for testing the Hosted canary rollout workflow end-to-end: feature gating → create a test Hosted route → create a baseline + candidate pair → configure a percentage rollout with guardrails → validate routing behavior (including streaming semantics) → validate telemetry + audit events → pause/rollback → cleanup.

Use this procedure for: (a) dogfooding the Console workflow, (b) verifying control-plane policy evaluation + propagation, and (c) validating data-plane routing behavior before beta/GA flag flips.

---

h2. Environments and URLs

* Console (staging): https://console.staging.redwoodinference.dev
* Hosted API (staging): https://api.staging.redwoodinference.dev
* Telemetry dashboards (staging Grafana): https://grafana.staging.redwoodinference.dev (SSO required)
* Audit log viewer (staging): https://security-audit.staging.redwoodinference.dev (restricted)

Notes:
* Staging uses separate policy propagation, routing clusters, and telemetry projects. Do not assume production dashboards/events are populated.
* If you are running from a local machine, ensure you are on VPN (or use bastion) so requests hit staging.

---

h2. Prerequisites

You need:
1) Staging account with Hosted enabled.
2) Entitlement to manage rollouts in staging.
3) RBAC permissions for rollout actions.
4) A pair of model identifiers you can route to in staging (baseline + candidate).

Minimum roles/permissions (staging):
* Hosted Route Admin (create/edit routes)
* Rollout Admin (create/edit/pause/rollback rollouts)
* Observability Viewer (view canary compare dashboards)

If you do not have these, file an internal helpdesk request and include your staging org + route name:
* INT request template: “Enable Hosted Rollouts (GA) dogfood for staging org + grant Rollout Admin.”

---

h2. Step 0 — Confirm feature gating (required)

The Hosted canary workflow in staging is behind both entitlement and feature flags. All three layers must be satisfied:

A) Entitlement (org-level)
* Entitlement key: hosted_rollouts_ga
* Expected values: enabled | disabled

B) Console feature flag (UI)
* Flag: console.hosted_rollouts_ga
* Controls visibility of Rollouts UI and wizard actions.

C) Control-plane feature flag (API)
* Flag: controlplane.rollout_policy_v2
* Controls acceptance of rollout_policy v2 schema and preview endpoint behavior.

How to verify quickly:
1) Open Console (staging) → your org → Settings → Feature access.
2) Confirm “Hosted Rollouts (GA)” is enabled.
3) Navigate to Hosted → Routes → select any route. You should see a “Rollouts” tab.

If the UI is missing but entitlement is enabled:
* Ask in #eng-platform with your org slug and confirm console.hosted_rollouts_ga is on for that org.

If the UI exists but create/save fails with schema/validation errors:
* Control-plane flag may be off. Check #eng-platform and reference “controlplane.rollout_policy_v2”.

---

h2. Step 1 — Create a dedicated staging test route

Create a route that is clearly identified as staging-only and safe for testing.

Recommended naming convention:
* Route name: canary-dogfood-<yourname>-<YYYYMMDD>
* Example: canary-dogfood-jada-20250203

Console steps:
1) Console (staging) → Hosted → Routes → Create route.
2) Route type: Chat (or Text Generation). Pick the one you intend to test.
3) Region: choose a single region for initial validation (recommended: us-east-stg). After validation, expand to 2 regions to test propagation.
4) Configure baseline model + version (see Step 2).
5) Save.

Validation:
* Confirm the route is callable and returns baseline responses.

---

h2. Step 2 — Choose baseline and candidate model/version pair

The canary workflow compares “baseline” vs “candidate”. For staging testing, pick a pair that is:
* Compatible with the route type (chat vs completion).
* Similar enough to not fail basic prompts.
* Distinct enough that you can tell which variant served the request.

Recommended test pairs (staging catalog; update if a model is deprecated):
* Baseline: ri/open-llm-8b@2025-01-15
* Candidate: ri/open-llm-8b@2025-02-01 (newer weights/serving profile)

If you need a more obvious difference for verification:
* Use a candidate with a different “system prompt” profile or tokenizer version (ask #eng-runtime if uncertain).

Important:
* Do not use experimental models that are known to spike latency or error rates unless you are explicitly testing guardrail triggers.

---

h2. Step 3 — Generate API key and set environment variables

1) Console (staging) → API Keys → Create key.
2) Scope: Hosted inference + Hosted route read (minimum) and Rollout management if you plan to use APIs.
3) Copy the key and export locally:

*Bash*
export RI_STAGING_API_KEY="<redacted>"
export RI_STAGING_API_BASE="https://api.staging.redwoodinference.dev"
export RI_ROUTE="canary-dogfood-jada-20250203"

Quick baseline call (chat example):

curl -sS "$RI_STAGING_API_BASE/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RI_STAGING_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "route": "'"$RI_ROUTE"'",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "system", "content": "You are a concise assistant."},
      {"role": "user", "content": "Reply with the single word: BASELINE"}
    ],
    "max_tokens": 16,
    "temperature": 0
  }'

Expected:
* 200 OK, response body present.
* No rollout headers yet (because rollout not created).

---

h2. Step 4 — Create the canary rollout in Console (wizard)

Console (staging) → Hosted → Routes → <your route> → Rollouts → Create rollout.

Wizard configuration (recommended for first end-to-end run):

1) Variants
* Baseline: (existing route target) ri/open-llm-8b@2025-01-15
* Candidate: ri/open-llm-8b@2025-02-01

2) Traffic split
* Start: 90% baseline / 10% candidate
* Stickiness: enabled
  * Strategy: request-hash (default)
  * Hash key: account_id + route_id + user_id (if provided)

3) Schedule
* Manual steps only (for first test)
* Define steps:
  * Step A: 10% candidate
  * Step B: 25% candidate
  * Step C: 50% candidate

4) Guardrails (set all to catch obvious issues)
* Error rate delta threshold:
  * Candidate 5xx rate must not exceed baseline by > 1.0% (rolling 5 min)
* Latency threshold:
  * Candidate p95 latency must not exceed baseline by > 200 ms (rolling 5 min)
* Token cost delta threshold:
  * Candidate input+output token cost must not exceed baseline by > 15% (rolling 15 min)
* Optional quality gate:
  * Leave OFF for first run unless you have a configured prompt set + eval pipeline in staging.

5) Safe defaults / confirmations
* Ensure the wizard shows a confirmation when candidate ≥ 50% (expected).
* Ensure “Start rollout” requires explicit confirmation.

Save and start.

Expected:
* Rollout shows status: Active.
* Current step: 10% candidate.
* Preview effective routing panel shows weights and selected stickiness setting.

---

h2. Step 5 — Validate routing behavior (non-streaming)

Goal: verify that weighted routing is applied by the data plane and that stickiness behaves as expected.

A) Quick smoke: observe both variants over many requests

Run 50 requests and look for variant distribution.

Recommended: include a user identifier to exercise stickiness.

for i in $(seq 1 50); do
  curl -sS "$RI_STAGING_API_BASE/v1/chat/completions" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $RI_STAGING_API_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{
      "route": "'"$RI_ROUTE"'",
      "user": "staging-dogfood-user-'"$i"'",
      "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"Say OK"}],
      "max_tokens": 8,
      "temperature": 0
    }' >/dev/null
  sleep 0.1
done

Expected:
* You should see metrics showing ~10% candidate (not necessarily exact).
* With stickiness enabled, repeated calls with the same “user” should consistently hit the same variant.

B) Verify “sticky” behavior explicitly

Pick a single user id and call repeatedly:

for i in $(seq 1 10); do
  curl -sS "$RI_STAGING_API_BASE/v1/chat/completions" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $RI_STAGING_API_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{
      "route": "'"$RI_ROUTE"'",
      "user": "staging-sticky-user-1",
      "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"Return a short UUID"}],
      "max_tokens": 16,
      "temperature": 0
    }' >/dev/null
done

How to confirm which variant served:
* Prefer telemetry dashboards (Step 7).
* If the route is configured to emit debug response headers in staging, check for:
  * x-ri-variant: baseline|candidate
  * x-ri-rollout-id: <uuid>
  * x-ri-policy-version: <int>

If you do not see headers, that is OK; use telemetry.

---

h2. Step 6 — Validate streaming/session semantics

Goal: ensure a streaming request is pinned to a single variant for the entire stream, and that retries reuse the same selection when applicable.

A) Start a streaming call

curl -N "$RI_STAGING_API_BASE/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RI_STAGING_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "route": "'"$RI_ROUTE"'",
    "user": "staging-stream-user-1",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "system", "content": "Stream your response."},
      {"role": "user", "content": "Count from 1 to 50 with commas."}
    ],
    "max_tokens": 200,
    "temperature": 0,
    "stream": true
  }'

Expected:
* Stream completes without mixing (no mid-stream model switches).

B) Retry behavior (controlled)

If you have a safe way to induce a client-side retry (e.g., terminate the curl connection mid-stream and retry immediately with the same request_id), do so.

Expected (per ADR-039):
* Variant selection is made at request start.
* If the client provides a stable idempotency key / request_id and the platform performs a retry, the selection should be consistent.

If you cannot reproduce retries safely, skip and rely on integration tests.

---

h2. Step 7 — Validate telemetry and canary comparison views

Goal: verify that per-variant metrics are emitted with the expected dimensions and that cardinality is controlled.

A) In Console
1) Route → Rollouts → open your active rollout.
2) Open “Monitoring” (or “Compare”) panel.
3) Confirm the following charts populate within 2–5 minutes:
* Requests (baseline vs candidate)
* Error rate (4xx/5xx)
* Latency p50/p95
* Token cost (input/output) and cost delta

B) In Grafana (staging)
Open the “Hosted Rollouts: Canary Compare” dashboard.
Filters:
* route = <your route>
* rollout_id = <your rollout>
* region = us-east-stg

Expected:
* Two time series sets (baseline/candidate).
* Candidate request volume ≈ configured percentage.

Cardinality checks:
* Ensure you are not producing per-user labels.
* Variant label should be low-cardinality and fixed: baseline|candidate.

If dashboards are empty after 10 minutes:
* Confirm you are hitting staging API base.
* Confirm telemetry pipeline for staging is healthy.
* Ask #observability with: route name, rollout id, timeframe, region.

---

h2. Step 8 — Validate policy propagation and “effective routing” preview

Goal: ensure control-plane policy version increments and data-plane picks up changes deterministically.

A) Change weights in the wizard
1) Route → Rollouts → Edit.
2) Move from Step A (10%) to Step B (25%) and save.

Expected:
* UI shows updated weights and a new activity entry.
* “Preview effective routing” reflects the new weights immediately in control plane.

B) Confirm propagation
Within the propagation SLO window (see related SLO page), confirm:
* Data-plane metrics shift toward ~25% candidate.

If metrics remain at the old split beyond the expected window:
* Check rollout policy version in the preview panel.
* Check “policy staleness” panel in the rollout-control-plane dashboard.
* Escalate to #eng-platform and include rollout id + region.

---

h2. Step 9 — Validate guardrails (optional but recommended)

Goal: confirm guardrail configuration is accepted, visible in UI, and can trigger (in staging) without causing broad disruption.

Two safe ways to validate guardrails without breaking shared staging:

Option A: Tighten thresholds temporarily
* Set latency delta threshold to 1 ms for candidate.
* Generate moderate traffic (e.g., 200 requests) and confirm the UI flags candidate as violating.
* Do NOT leave unrealistic thresholds in place.

Option B: Candidate with known slower profile (only if approved)
* Use a candidate profile with slightly higher latency and verify the delta shows up.
* Coordinate in #eng-runtime to avoid noisy staging.

Expected:
* Guardrail status appears in Console.
* Monitoring view highlights deltas.
* No automatic rollback occurs unless explicitly enabled (depending on current staging behavior).

---

h2. Step 10 — Pause and rollback

Goal: ensure the pause/rollback flows work and routing returns to baseline.

A) Pause
1) Route → Rollouts → Pause rollout.
2) Confirm confirmation dialog is shown.

Expected:
* Rollout status: Paused.
* Effective routing returns to 100% baseline (or the configured “pause behavior” if different in your build).

B) Rollback
1) Route → Rollouts → Rollback to baseline.
2) Confirm warning messaging is shown.

Expected:
* Candidate weight becomes 0%.
* New activity/audit entry created.
* Within propagation window, candidate traffic drops to ~0.

Operational reference:
* If you need to force baseline immediately during an incident simulation, follow the runbook: “Hosted rollout pause and rollback runbook”.

---

h2. Step 11 — Validate audit logging (restricted)

Goal: confirm that rollout lifecycle events produce audit entries with correct actor attribution and before/after diffs.

Audit event types to look for:
* rollout.created
* rollout.updated
* rollout.paused
* rollout.rolled_back

Procedure:
1) Open the audit log viewer (staging) or query in SIEM staging export (if you have access).
2) Filter by route id or rollout id.
3) Confirm:
* Actor matches your SSO identity.
* Event contains org id, route id, rollout id.
* Diff is present for update events (before/after weights, guardrails, schedule).
* No prompt text or user content is included.

If you do not have access:
* Ask #eng-security with rollout id and timeframe; they can confirm events exist.

---

h2. Cleanup

After validation, clean up to avoid cluttering staging:
1) Delete/disable the rollout.
2) Delete the staging test route.
3) Revoke the API key if it was created for this test only.

If you need the route for repeated testing, rename it to include “persistent” and add an owner note in the route description.

---

h2. Troubleshooting

* “Rollouts tab is missing”
  * Check entitlement hosted_rollouts_ga and flag console.hosted_rollouts_ga.

* “403 Forbidden when creating/editing rollout”
  * Missing RBAC permission. Ask for Rollout Admin or specific permissions (create/edit/pause/rollback).

* “Validation error: weights”
  * Weights must sum to 100.
  * Candidate weight = 100% may require additional confirmation/guardrails depending on build.

* “Traffic split doesn’t change after editing”
  * Check policy propagation dashboard for staleness.
  * Confirm you are looking at the same region.
  * If multi-region, confirm all regions converge.

* “Streaming response appears to switch behavior mid-stream”
  * This is a P0 bug for canaries. Capture request_id (if available), timestamps, and share with #eng-runtime and #eng-platform.

* “Dashboards show data but Console compare is empty”
  * Likely a Console query or permissions issue. Capture rollout id + screenshot and file a Console bug.

---

h2. What to attach to bug reports

When filing a bug (Linear/Jira), include:
* Org slug, route name, rollout id
* Region(s)
* Approx timeframe (UTC)
* Current weights + stickiness settings
* Whether requests were streaming
* Screenshots of Console “Preview effective routing” and “Activity” timeline
* Links to Grafana panels (staging)

---

h2. Appendix — Suggested staging test matrix

Run at least one pass for each row:

| Scenario | What you’re validating | Expected result |
|---|---|---|
| 10% candidate, stickiness ON | basic weighted split + consistent user mapping | stable mapping per user, aggregate ~10% |
| 25% candidate, stickiness OFF | pure weighted random | aggregate ~25%, per-user may vary |
| Streaming request | variant pinning for full stream | no cross-variant mixing |
| Pause | emergency stop semantics | candidate traffic drops to ~0 quickly |
| Rollback | return to baseline + audit | baseline 100%, audit events present |

End.
